row.evidence: dmarcian's pricing table lists Single Sign On only on Enterprise and no SCIM or provisioning row; its SSO guide says you have to add the users allowed to log in through your IdP, and Microsoft's dmarcian tutorial says 'In dmarcian, provisioning is a manual task.'
row.notes: Status changed from gated to none: June said SCIM was on Enterprise (~$499/mo), but no first-party page mentions SCIM on 2026-10-05; the Entra tutorial says provisioning is manual and the Okta OIN app is SWA-only. Flat pricing by domains and message volume, so per-user fields are null (June's normalised ~$2/u/mo dropped). Annual prices: Basic $239.88/yr ($19.99/mo), Plus $2,388/yr ($199/mo), Enterprise $5,988/yr ($499/mo); monthly billing is $24/$240/$600 per month. Basic allows 1 user, Plus 3, Enterprise unlimited. SAML SSO and API Access are Enterprise-only; the API is not publicly documented.

plans.name: Basic
plans.notes: 1 user, up to 2 active domains. Monthly billing $24/mo.

plans.name: Plus
plans.notes: 3 users, up to 8 active domains, User Access Controls. Monthly billing $240/mo.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Unlimited users, up to 15 active domains, API Access (undocumented publicly), SAML SSO. Monthly billing $600/mo.

scim.notes: No SCIM on the pricing table, SSO guide or site sitemap; Microsoft's tutorial says provisioning is manual. Left null rather than false because dmarcian itself never says 'no SCIM'.

user_api.notes: Pricing lists 'API Access' on Enterprise only and the glossary describes it as programmatic access to reports and data; the API (us.dmarcian.com/api/) requires credentials and no public reference with user-management endpoints was found.

limitations.text: API Access is an Enterprise-only feature; public docs describe only report/data access.

okta.notes: OIN page marks only SWA (page markup); dmarcian's guide uses a custom SAML app in Okta.

fallbacks.notes: Users must be added in Manage Settings > User Management before they can sign in with SSO.

open_questions: June's 'SCIM on Enterprise' claim has no first-party source; dmarcian may offer it privately on Custom contracts.
Whether the Enterprise API includes user-management endpoints (no public reference).
Google, OneLogin and JumpCloud catalogue listings were not checked.
